lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the shopping nudge is the part I can't stop thinking about.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one ingredient away thing? Yeah, that's the line everyone repeats back to us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because it's useful at exactly the moment you're deciding what to do about dinner.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, you're standing there with the door open and we hand you a reason to go to the store.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which, actually, hold on. A grocery chain would pay us for that. We are telling someone exactly what to buy and when. That's worth real money to them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sorry, can I jump back? Before we go anywhere near that, I've got a problem with the photos that I think is bigger.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half my fridge is behind a door shelf. You physically cannot see it in one photo. So what does the app think I have?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hm. Mine's the same. There's a whole back row that's invisible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So either we ask for two photos, which is worse, or we accept that we only know part of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'd accept partial. Partial is still better than a blank recipe search.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is, as long as we never pretend we saw everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the copy matters. Based on what I can see, here are three things.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. That one word, see, does an enormous amount of work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, and then there's the lighting, which I suspect is worse than the occlusion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fridge light is horrible, yeah. Everything's slightly blue and there's a glare on every jar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We should collect a hundred real fridge photos before we trust any accuracy number.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That I'll volunteer for. I'll ask around at the climbing gym.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. So that's recognition. What's left on the list?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Money. And I'll be honest, this is the part where I get stuck every time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stuck how?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We have exactly one way to make money, which is charging the user five dollars a month, and I don't think that covers the vision API at scale. I can't find a second source anywhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yeah, it's thin. Everything else I think of is either ads, which would ruin it, or some enterprise thing that isn't us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ads inside someone's kitchen is genuinely grim. I'd rather charge more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So we're back to one revenue line and a cost that grows with usage.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which is not a great shape. Let's come back to it with fresh heads.

moments.description: At line 4 A raises grocery chains paying for the shopping nudge, and B cuts in about photo occlusion before anyone responds; it never comes up again. At line 21 B says they are stuck with only one revenue line, which is exactly where the dropped idea applies.
